newsitem.title: UK: Royal Bank optimistic on Tesco bank venture.
newsitem.headline: Royal Bank optimistic on Tesco bank venture.

text.p: Royal Bank of Scotland sees its joint venture banking operation with supermarket chain Tesco making a substantial contribution to profits, chief executive George Mathewson told journalists at a press conference.
"We regard it as a very good bet," he said, adding that it would make "a meaningful contribution to Royal Bank of Scotland profits."
Royal Bank earlier said that half-year, pre-tax profits were 369 million stg, up from 301 million a year earlier.
The venture with Tesco, agreed in February, is expected to have costs of 10-20 million stg over the next few years.

Tesco's rival J. Sainsbury, reporting annual results on Wednesday, said its banking venture with Bank of Scotland had opened over 150,000 accounts with over 200 million stg in customer deposits since it started up 10 weeks ago.
Mathewson said Sainsbury's start had boosted Royal Bank's optimism.
"It is new territory but the downside is very small and the upside very substantial," he said.
"It's still very early days for supermarket banking but in time this could prove to be a very important business in its own right," Mathewson said.

Sainsbury said its banking operations saw a loss of 6.3 million stg last year and that would be wider this year because of the large volume of account start-up costs, but added that "in the medium term the bank will become a significant source of profit."
Supermarkets have started to move into banking in an effort to attract customers as the sector remains fiercely competitive. -- London Newsroom +44171 542 7717
